title: “Zum zum zum” by Sylvie Vartan
text: "Zum zum zum" is a song written by Bruno Canfora and Antonio Amurri as an opening theme for the 1968 television program Canzonissima, when all the participants performed it in chorus. The song was originally recorded by Italian singer Mina, who was the host of the show.

title: “Scende la pioggia” by Gianni Morandi
text: "Elenore" is a 1968 song by the Turtles, originally included on The Turtles Present the Battle of the Bands. Although written by Howard Kaylan, its writing was co-credited to all five members of the band: Kaylan, Mark Volman, Al Nichol, Jim Pons, and John Barbata.

title: “Zingara” by Bobby Solo
text: "Zingara" is a song composed by Enrico Riccardi and Luigi Albertelli. The song won the nineteenth edition of the Sanremo Music Festival, with a double performance by Bobby Solo and Iva Zanicchi.

title: “Ma che freddo fa” by Nada
text: "Ma che freddo fa" is a 1969 song composed by Claudio Mattone (music) and Franco Migliacci (lyrics). The song premiered at the 19th edition of the Sanremo Music Festival with a double performance of Nada and The Rokes, placing at the fifth place.

title: “Eloise” by Barry Ryan
text: "Eloise" is a song first released in 1968 on the MGM label. It was performed by English singer Barry Ryan and written by his twin brother, Paul Ryan.

title: “Tutta mia la città” by Equipe 84
text: "Blackberry Way" is a 1968 single by British band The Move. Written by the band's guitarist/vocalist Roy Wood and produced by Jimmy Miller, "Blackberry Way" was a bleak counterpoint to the sunny psychedelia of earlier recordings.

title: “Storia d'amore” by Adriano Celentano
text: Adriano Celentano is an Italian singer-songwriter, actor, showman, and filmmaker. He is dubbed Il Molleggiato ('the springy one') because of his energetic dancing.

title: “Pensando a te” by Al Bano
text: Albano Antonio Carrisi, better known as Al Bano, is an Italian singer and actor. Having sold over 25 million records globally and career spanning seven decades, he is one of the most recognisable Italian singers in the world.

title: “Lisa dagli occhi blu” by Mario Tessuto
text: "Lisa dagli occhi blu" is a 1969 Italian song composed by Claudio Cavallaro (music) and Giancarlo Bigazzi (lyrics) and performed by Mario Tessuto. It is included in his debut album Lisa dagli occhi blu.
listen: Lisa dagli occhi blu Mario Tessuto

title: “Pensiero d'amore” by Mal
text: "I've Gotta Get a Message to You" is a song by the Bee Gees. Released as a single in 1968, it was their second number-one hit in the UK Singles Chart, and their first US Top 10 hit.
wiki: I've Gotta Get a Message to You

title: “Il primo giorno di primavera” by Dik Dik
text: "Il primo giorno di primavera" is a 1969 song composed by Mario Lavezzi, Cristiano Minellono and Mogol and performed by the musical group Dik Dik. title: “Lo straniero” by Georges Moustaki
text: "Le métèque" is a French chanson by Georges Moustaki. He wrote it in 1969, and it was his first breakthrough hit, reaching number one in the French charts for six non-consecutive weeks.

title: “Belinda” by Gianni Morandi
text: "Pretty Belinda" is a song written and recorded by Chris Andrews, which he released as a single in July 1969.

title: After 147 years, the last issue of The Saturday Evening Post in its original form appears in the United States.
text: The Saturday Evening Post is an American magazine published six times a year. It was first published in 1821, and published weekly from 1897 until 1963.

title: German-born writer Assia Wevill, a mistress of the English poet Ted Hughes and ex-wife of the Canadian poet David Wevill, gasses herself and their 4-year-old daughter Alexandra Tatiana Elise "Shura" Wevill at her London home.
text: Edward James Hughes was an English poet, translator, and children's writer. Critics frequently rank him as one of the best poets of his generation and one of the twentieth century's greatest writers.

title: The first Booker-McConnell Prize for fiction is awarded to P. H. Newby for Something to Answer For.
text: The Booker Prize, formerly the Booker Prize for Fiction and the Man Booker Prize (2002–2019), is a literary award conferred each year for the best single work of sustained English fiction which was published in the United Kingdom or Ireland. title: "Penelope Ashe", purported author of a bestselling novel, Naked Came the Stranger, is revealed as a group of Newsday journalists.The book was co-written by a group of twenty-four journalists which was led by the Newsday columnist Mike…
text: Newsday is a daily newspaper in the United States primarily serving Nassau and Suffolk counties on Long Island, New York, although it is also sold throughout the New York metropolitan area. The slogan of the newspaper is "Your Eye on LI", and formerly it was "The Long Island Newspaper".

title: unknown date – The Times Literary Supplement begins using the abbreviation "TLS" on its title page.
text: The Times Literary Supplement is a fortnightly literary review published in London by News UK, a subsidiary of News Corp.
